encoder: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5), a single agent working alone in each of two passes (pass 1 from BRIEF-pass1.md, pass 2 the completion pass to whole), with no subagents
display_name: Interpretation Act 2005 (Ireland): the whole Act as executable rules, including time, commencement, construction, powers and duties, the Schedule's defined words and repeal, refusing where the Act is silent

l4_bin.note: check.sh was run with L4_TARGET=unstable (the default in this row's check.sh); the brief requires @lang en, REFUSE and YMD, which main rejects, so no main comparison was made. Pass 1 ran on a binary that printed 'dev'; the 16 pass-1 modules print the same numbers on both.

source.kind: unofficial plain-text rendering of the English enacted text; not the official text

scope.encoded: Every provision of the English text, one coverage-table row per unit (256 units, NOTES.md section 4): ss 1(2) to 27 (this Act's commencement; interpretation and deemed repeal; repeals and savings; application and contrary intention; construing obscure, ambiguous or absurd provisions and provisions in changing circumstances; the text a court may use; summary proceedings when Acts are read together; references to Parts and divisions; an enactment always speaking; examples; deviation from a form; judicial notice; citation, citation of amended enactments and omitted commas; the date of passing and the Clerk's endorsement; commencement; powers exercised before commencement; all of s 18 (a) to (j) with the hour offset of (i) asked as an input; statutory instruments; interpretation provisions; the Schedule's words in an enactment; powers and duties, including the holder for the time being of an office; rules of court; service by post; repeals and substitutions; effect of repeal); the Schedule's Part 1 (32 words) and Part 2 (8 words) as a defined-term table with appliers for the entries that include, exclude or carry a condition; and the 'Acts Referred to' table (18 rows).
scope.inert: 80 units not operative (file header, titles, long title, date of enactment, enacting words, Part and section headings and marginal notes, the arrangement of sections, the Schedule heading and cross-reference) and 1 unit of machinery (the short title, s 1(1)); none repealed or blank.
scope.refuses: where the Act has no rule: a period of months or years that does not begin on the first day of the unit; a period of weeks that does not begin on a Sunday; any period counted after an event; a last day that falls on a day of rest, recess or holiday; the moment of commencement under s 16(1); a Saorstat Eireann statute silent on commencement; a time of service once the contrary is proved; an hour outside 0 to 23 (s 18(i)); a time expressed by hour when no offset is supplied; a party of another kind (s 18(c)); an offence punishable in another way (s 18(j)); two holders of one office on one day (ss 22(2), 23(2)); a different date endorsed, and the time limit of 'immediately' (s 15(2)); an Act passed on 1 January 1801 (pre-union Irish statute); a Schedule entry's 'includes' or 'does not include' list for a thing it does not name; a word in an instrument where a contrary intention appears (s 19).
scope.asked_as_inputs: a calendar of public holidays (Organisation of Working Time Act 1997); the offset of the standard time of a day (Standard Time (Amendment) Act 1971); how a person attains an age; that a court is as established by law; the content of the other enactments that Schedule entries point at; the judgments the Act leaves to the reader (obscure or ambiguous, absurd, plain intention, materially affects, as occasion requires).
scope.readings_not_the_acts: ie-month-year-readings.l4 holds the alternative readings (clamped corresponding date, first day included, rolled corresponding date, seven-day week, roll-forward off a rest day); the Act's own modules never call it.

checks.diagnostics: 90 Hints across 26 files, all the @lang en Hint; no Warning; the only Errors are the eight in tests-red-control.l4
checks.note: Re-run on 2026-10-29 after the three edits that fixed the includes lookup (NOTES.md finding 13, fork F48): only tests-schedule-definitions.l4 moved, 383 to 421 satisfied; the 8 expected failures are unchanged. Before the fixes the same run gave 1284 satisfied.

with_independent_tests.note: tests-independent.l4 alone: 362 satisfied, 0 failed, 0 refused. Written by a separate agent from the source text before it opened any .l4; see NOTES.md section 11.

not_reviewed: No domain expert has read this encoding against the statute. It was written by one agent, in two passes, from the unofficial plain-text rendering of the enacted text and checked only by its own tests, the self-check in check.sh and the quotation gate; no second reader has compared it with the official text of the Act, the Irish-language text was not consulted, and the word, part, kind of meaning and case in the Part A tests of the Schedule were extracted from the text by a script.
